newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts react to Mercedes chief departure.
newsitem.headline: Analysts react to Mercedes chief departure.

text.p: Analysts made the following comments on news that Mercedes-Benz AG chairman Helmut Werner is to leave the Daimler-Benz AG group
Peter Schmidt, Automotive Industry Data, U.K.
"This is a good move for Daimler and a good move for Mercedes shareholders. It is not surprising, you don't need me to tell you that there has been a power struggle between Werner and Schrempp.
"There wasn't room for Werner and Schrempp in the one company. Schrempp had to get clear and undisputed control.

"Werner is a very capable guy but he ran Mercedes as though it was his own company and an autonomous group and this just is not the case. In this day and age this is not the way any large multinational can go".
London-based auto analyst (speaking on condition of anonymity)
"I think there will be very little change. The general direction has already been sketched out.
"At the end of the day I think first of all that it is unfortunate to lose Werner.

"Looking at Werner's record, he's being viewed as the architect of the revival (at Mercedes). But one has to say that part of this is due to Mercedes going through a normal cycle and the success of the E class (car).
"The thing is that Schrempp had time on his hands. Once they got rid of Fokker and the other problem children, they basically have Airbus and Mercedes left.
There is not much active management and the key driver will be Mercedes.
German auto industry analyst (speaking on condition of anonymity)
"A good man has been driven out of the business."
"The question is still whether Daimler should meddle with Mercedes.
"In the coming years, the decisions have already been taken and we will not see the impact of Werner's departure for some time."
